pr_title: Accounting for the position quantity in margin requirements
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

When shorting options and options strategies with no initial holdings, the margin buying power model allowed us to short too many contracts, making us go avobe the available margin. This is because it was using the existing security holdings to calculate the margin requirements for any existing or potential position.

This fixes this by pssing the actual quantity down to the margin requirement calculation method.

- Quantity is reduced in initial orders when there are no holdings, because the models where allowing highier quantities than actually margin was available for. For some algorithms, the order quantities were reduced to match this, as well as cash was increased for some others for them to be able to hold the positions.
- Note about `Algorithm.CSharp/OptionChainConsistencyRegressionAlgorithm.cs`: the orders list hash changed. The reason is the following: this algorithm runs for a single day, placing a market order and then liquidating it on market close. Right after that, the condition `!Portfolio.Invested` is true again, so the orders are placed again but never filled because the algorithm is completed. The last MOC order is invalidated with this changes because of insufficient buying power, hence the hash change.

##### Shorting options outside of margin in IB for validation

issue_context.title: Cannot liquidate part of an option strategy naked short position
issue_context.body: #### Expected Behavior When holding a naked short position for an option strategy, the algorithm is able to liquidate part of that position. #### Actual Behavior When holding a naked short position for an option strategy (say `group quantity=-5`), the algorithm is not able to place a reverting order to liquidate part of the position (`quantity < |strategyQuantity|`. E.g. `quantity = 4` in this case). #### Potential Solution A potential hint: look into the `PositionGroupBuyingPowerModel`, specifically into how the available and delta buying power are calculated in [`HasSufficientBuyingPowerForOrder`](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/4d3211957631e085fe299c8452c794c180a4f165/Common/Securities/Positions/PositionGroupBuyingPowerModel.cs#L142), which is used by the transaction handler to check where an order can be submitted and filled. The condition `deltaBuyingPower <= availableBuyingPower` is not met for this cases, resulting in unsufficient buying power. #### Reproducing the Problem Run this algorithm: ```python import itertools class SleepyTanMule(QCAlgorithm): def Initialize(self): self.SetStartDate(2015, 12, 24) self.SetEndDate(2015, 12, 24) self.SetCash(150000) equity = self.AddEquity("GOOG", leverage=4) option = self.AddOption(equity.Symbol) self._optionSymbol = option.Symbol option.SetFilter(lambda u: u.Strikes(-2, +2).Expiration(0, 180)) def OnData(self, data): if not self.Portfolio.Invested: for chain in data.OptionChains.Values: callContracts = [contract for contract in chain if contract.Right == OptionRight.Call] callContracts = [(key, list(group)) for key, group in itertools.groupby(callContracts, key=lambda x: x.Expiry)] callContracts.sort(key=lambda x: x[0]) callContracts = callContracts[0][1] callContracts.sort(key=lambda x: x.Strike) if len(callContracts) < 3: break expiry = callContracts[0].Expiry lowerStrike = callContracts[0].Strike middleStrike = callContracts[1].Strike higherStrike = callContracts[2].Strike self._optionStrategy = OptionStrategies.Straddle(self._optionSymbol, higherStrike, expiry) self._strategyQuantity = -5 self.Order(self._optionStrategy, self._strategyQuantity) else: self.Order(self._optionStrategy, abs(self._strategyQuantity) - 1) ``` Se the orders and logs: #### System Information Local environment in Windows 11 and QC Cloud #### Checklist - [x] I have completely filled out this template - [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch - [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues) - [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue
